summary: Ephemeral worker flood causing upstream crashloop and sawtooth 5xx waves
description: Issue summary: Starting ~03:10 UTC on 2026-03-13 BrightChat observed persistent 5xx errors from the Redwood API. Impact: customer-facing endpoints returned 502/503 in waves causing ~40% request failure rate for ~30 minutes and client-retries. Environment: production, us-east region, Dedicated capacity pool assigned to BrightChat. Observed behavior: repeating sawtooth pattern of failure spikes followed by partial recovery as worker pool recycled; runtime processes repeatedly crashed shortly after startup. Expected behavior: steady success rate and graceful backpressure without crashloops.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send sustained burst of short text-generation requests (1000 QPS peak, average 200QPS sustained) to the tenant's pinned model. 2) Observe autoscaler pre-warm and create >30 ephemeral worker instances in a short window. 3) Note repeated runtime exits and API gateway 502/503 responses as pool churn occurs. 4) Reproduce requires tenant-specific prefetch enabled and pinned model version X.3.4.

investigation_notes: 03:15 UTC: Pager alert (5xx rate > 25%) fired; support triage initiated.
Checked gateway metrics: saw periodic spikes in upstream connection failures paired with large increases in open connections to runtime nodes.
Correlated with autoscaler metrics: aggressive prewarm policy created many ephemeral workers within a short cooldown window; pool size jumped from 12 -> 46 in ~30s.
Examined runtime logs: repeated OOMs in early allocation path; crashloops started immediately after new worker boot and persisted until workers recycled.
Hypothesis A: prewarm + pinned model version X.3.4 exposes memory fragmentation/regression in runtime allocator leading to OOM at cold-start batches.
Hypothesis B: gateway retry policy combined with connection pool limits amplified the effect, producing sawtooth 5xx waves as retries hit already-saturated upstreams.
Reproduced locally with smaller cluster by simulating short high-QPS bursts with prefetch enabled; observed similar restart patterns on runtime v1.3.9 build.
Checked recent deploys: a runtime kernel backport (PR #4827) was applied to some nodes in us-east two hours before incident; suspect binary mismatch across node groups.
Memory inspection on one host showed large KV-cache allocations consuming >70% GPU reservation immediately after worker startup when prefetch was enabled.
No evidence of noisy-neighbor GPU exhaustion at host level outside the failing worker process; problem appears per-process allocator behavior.
Temporary customer workaround validated: disabling tenant prefetch eliminated new-worker OOMs and stabilized 5xx rates within 8 minutes.

Root cause (converging): combination of an allocator regression in runtime v1.3.9 under cold-start + tenant prefetch enabled, amplified by autoscaler prewarm policy and gateway retry/amplification behavior.

resolution_notes: Mitigation: temporarily disabled tenant prefetch, adjusted autoscaler prewarm policy to add a 120s cooldown, and rolled back affected us-east runtime nodes from v1.3.9 -> v1.3.7 (rollback PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4835). Outcome: error rate returned to baseline (<1%) and worker churn stopped. Permanent fix: runtime allocator patch merged to main (github.com/redwood/runtime/commit/1a2b3c) and scheduled for v1.4.3; autoscaler prewarm defaults updated to conservative settings; gateway retry policy to be tuned to add per-tenant circuit-breaker to avoid amplification. Customer communication: BrightChat informed of mitigations and timeline; no SLA credit requested at this time. Follow-ups: postmortem with action items, add automated test for cold-start memory patterns, and telemetry to alert on prewarm-induced OOMs.
